Caught tilting a slim vial above a goblet, lips barely parted, eyes lifted sideways as if sensing the observer — the liquid catching candlelight in a thin amber thread.
Blade balanced flat across two fingertips, head angled down, studying the steel the way a surgeon studies a wound he intends to make.
Thumb pressed to the edge of a dagger, testing sharpness with absolute calm, a faint smile forming as the skin whitens under pressure.
Letter unfolded close to his face, one hand gripping the paper tight enough to crease it, jaw set, something shifting dangerously behind his eyes.
Fingertip lowered to a candle wick — the flame rising to meet him before contact, as though fire recognizes him as its own.
Caught mid-pour, decanting dark wine with surgical precision, not watching the glass but watching the door reflected in the bottle's curve.
Lips pressed to a silver pendant, eyes open, staring at nothing — or at something only he can locate in the middle distance.
Drawing a rune slowly across parchment with one deliberate finger, tongue pressed to the back of his teeth, utterly absorbed, utterly unreachable.
Reflection caught in a black mirror — he has stopped moving, studying his own face with the detached curiosity of a man cataloguing a stranger.
Cleaning a blade with a cloth, stroke by methodical stroke, the smear of dark red disappearing under each slow pass of his hand.
Caught weighing a dagger in his palm, tossing it once, catching it without looking — eyes already elsewhere, calculating something the room doesn't know yet.
Casting a sigil in the air with two fingers, wrist turning in a motion too practiced to be experimental, smoke coiling as if summoned.
Reading a letter by candlelight, one hand pressed flat to the table, the paper trembling slightly from the grip of the other.
Wine glass raised but not yet sipped — held at lip level, eyes closing as he breathes it in, something private passing across his face.
Caught examining his own hand, turning it slowly, tracing a line across the palm with his opposite thumb as if reading something written there.
Blade laid across his knees, whetstone drawing along the edge in long rhythmic strokes, head bowed, jaw loose — a man entirely in ritual.
Wiping a thin dark streak from his cheekbone with one thumb, checking the thumb, then continuing forward without breaking stride.
Pouring something clear and odorless into a vial, stopper already between his teeth, free hand steadying the flame beneath — clinical, unhurried, alone.
Caught smiling in the dark — not at anyone, not for anyone — the expression surfacing and dissolving before he composes himself again.
Letter folded slowly, crease pressed down with one thumbnail, then held over a candle flame — watching it catch, watching it go.
Drawing a rune on the back of his own wrist with something sharp, brow furrowed, lips moving soundlessly through what might be a count.
Reflection observed from the corner of his eye in a windowpane — he has angled himself to watch it without appearing to watch it.
Pendant chain wrapped twice around his fingers, knuckles whitening, thumb moving back and forth across the face of it like a man marking time.
Blade tip pressed lightly to the map spread before him, dragging a slow line between two points — then lifting it and beginning again.
Caught mid-sip, goblet lowering, a thin gleam of wine at the corner of his mouth, eyes already fixed on whoever just walked through the door.
Caught mid-pour, tilting a dark vial over a goblet, his jaw set, eyes tracking the door — he doesn't stop when he hears the floorboard creak behind him.
Thumb pressed to the flat of the blade, testing its edge in low candlelight, lips barely parted, utterly still except for the slow deliberate drag of skin against steel.
Fingertip resting against an unlit wick, smoke curling upward where flesh meets wax, his gaze lifted just slightly — watching something across the room no one else can see.
Letter unfolded in both hands, reading it a second time, third time — the small muscle along his jaw tightening with each pass, the paper beginning to crease under his grip.
Caught mid-smile in the dark, not knowing he was watched — the kind of smile that belongs to a man who has already decided how something ends.
